lesson: Many birds fly far between their summer and winter homes, and why: white storks ride rising warm air over land, by day, to where there is food in winter.

pages.art: Late summer in a cool northern country: green fields, a marsh with reeds, a village rooftop with a big round stork nest of sticks. On the nest stands Long-Legs, a young white stork (white body, black wing feathers, long red legs and a long red beak, a little scruffy, the beak still slightly darker than an adult's). In the pale sky above the fields, a great loose circle of storks, drawn as one stork silhouette repeated in a turning ring. Feeling: the end of summer, something about to begin. Calm area: the pale sky across the top, above the circling ring.

On the edge of a field, Long-Legs stands beside a big stork (taller, neater feathers, a bright red beak, calm eyes), looking up at her. The big stork has her beak pointed up as she clatters it. Behind them, the marsh is still and grey; a few dry reeds. Feeling: a question, a gentle answer. Calm area: the grey sky across the top.

Long-Legs just above the field, flapping hard, feathers ruffled, a few little motion lines; he is barely off the ground and his legs dangle. The big stork stands below on the grass, watching, head tilted. Feeling: effort, comic frustration. Calm area: the empty sky across the top.

Early morning: a line of storks standing still on a field and on a fence, waiting. The low sun has just cleared the hills and lights the ground gold. Above the brightest patch of field, the rising warm air is shown as a few faint, wavy, transparent stripes curling upward in a tall column, like heat shimmer made visible. Feeling: patience, a secret about to be shown. Calm area: the sky across the top, beside the shimmer.

Inside the invisible tower: the big stork and Long-Legs circling upward with wings spread wide and still, the faint wavy stripes of warm air turning around them; below, the fields grow smaller. Long-Legs' eyes are wide with delight. Feeling: lift, joy, wonder. Calm area: the open sky at the top.

A wide view across the sky: on the left, a tall spiral of storks (one silhouette repeated, turning); from its top, a long line of storks gliding down and away to the right, necks stretched forward, towards a second spiral far away. The land below in flat bands of green and brown. Feeling: the rhythm of the journey: up, glide, up. Calm area: the plain sky across the top.

The flock at the edge of the land: below them a curving shore, and beyond it a wide, flat, blue sea in layered bands reaching to the horizon, with no birds over it. Long-Legs leans towards the sea; the big stork turns along the shore, and the flock bends after her. Feeling: a wise choice. Calm area: the sky above the sea, across the top.

Evening: storks resting in a field and on a tall bare tree, many standing on one leg with their beaks tucked down on their chests. Long-Legs on a low branch, eyes half closed. The sky deep blue with the first stars. Feeling: rest, safety, a long day done. Calm area: the night sky across the top.

A tall picture of the land below changing, seen from above in horizontal bands from top to bottom: dark green forest with a river, then brown rolling hills, then pale dry fields and a few small white houses. A short line of storks gliding across the middle. Feeling: distance, days passing. Calm area: a plain band of pale sky across the top.

A green valley between brown hills, its floor a patchwork of rectangular fishponds shining silver and blue, with green fields between them. A great white spiral of storks (one silhouette repeated) is coming down into the valley; many already stand at the edges of the ponds. Feeling: arrival, plenty. Calm area: the sky above the hills, across the top.

On a dry grassy hill above the valley, in the shade of a small tree, a girl kneels with binoculars to her eyes; her grandfather sits beside her on a folding stool with a notebook open on his knee, drawing tally marks (four upright lines and one across, no digits). Below them, the valley of ponds and storks. Afternoon light. Feeling: excitement, sharing. Calm area: the sky across the top.

Split picture: on the left, close on the notebook page filling up with rows of tally gates (four lines and one across), the girl's pencil moving. On the right, down by a pond, Long-Legs standing on one leg, looking up towards the hill; the girl, small on the hilltop, lowers her binoculars and waves. Feeling: a meeting without words. Calm area: the sky above the hill, across the top.

Morning in the valley: the ponds pale and misty, then sun on the field. Long-Legs, first, wings spread, rising in a turn; behind and below him the other storks lift into the same spiral. The faint wavy stripes of warm air turn around them. Feeling: confidence, he knows the way now. Calm area: the sky across the top.

Last picture of the book: the girl and her grandfather on the hill, seen from behind, looking up at a slow white spiral of storks drifting away to the south in the morning sky. The girl holds her open notebook against her chest; on the open page is her own small drawing of a stork. Feeling: goodbye and hope. Calm area: the sky across the top.

shots.action: 12 s. Scene 1, the north. Wide on green fields and a marsh in cool late-summer light; a village roof with a big stick nest. The camera drifts slowly towards the nest. No words. Keep the lower fifth calm for captions in every shot.
sound: a slow, airy tune on a wooden flute

shots.action: 10 s. Long-Legs on the nest, stretching his long legs, wobbling, then standing proud.
10 s. He looks up: a great ring of storks circles over the fields (one silhouette repeated in a turning ring), clattering their beaks.
sound: many beaks clattering, like soft wooden rattles

shots.action: 8 s. The ring of storks passes over the nest; its shadow slides over the roof. Long-Legs ducks, then looks up again, curious. No words.
9 s. On the edge of the field, Long-Legs stands beside the big stork and looks up at her.
11 s. The big stork lifts her beak and clatters, then answers. The camera looks past her at the still marsh and the dry reeds.
8 s. Long-Legs flaps as hard as he can: up a little, down again, up a little. Comic, no words.
7 s. He lands in a heap, puffing.
7 s. The big stork tilts her head and looks at the sky.
10 s. Scene 2, the warm air. Dawn: storks stand still on the cold field and on a fence, waiting. Nobody moves. A breath, no words.
12 s. The sun clears the hills and lights the ground gold. Above the brightest patch, faint wavy stripes appear and begin to turn and rise in a tall, slow column: the warm air made visible.
6 s. The big stork opens her wings.

12 s. The big stork steps into the column and is carried up in slow circles without one flap; Long-Legs follows, wings wide and still, and rises too. The camera turns with them as the fields shrink below.
sound: the tune swells, turning like a waltz

shots.action: 8 s. Close on Long-Legs' face in the turning air: eyes wide, delighted. No words.
sound: a happy trill in the flute

shots.action: 12 s. At the top of the tower, the storks are tiny specks. They stretch out their necks and glide south in a long, slanting line, down and down, towards the next turning tower far away.
10 s. Rhythm of the journey in one smooth move: circle up, glide down, circle up again, the flock drawn as one repeated silhouette. No words.
sound: the waltz tune, up and down

shots.action: 9 s. Scene 3, the sea. The land ends in a curving shore; beyond it, a flat blue sea in layered bands, all the way to the sky. No birds over it.
6 s. Long-Legs tilts towards the sea, eager.
9 s. Over the water the warm-air stripes are missing: the air lies flat and still. The big stork turns along the shore and answers.
8 s. The whole flock bends after her and follows the coastline, a long white curve. No words.
10 s. Scene 4, evening. The air cools, the warm towers fade, and the storks come down to a field and a tall bare tree.
10 s. Storks on one leg, beaks tucked down; Long-Legs on a low branch, eyes closing. The first stars come out. A breath, no words.
sound: a soft lullaby phrase on the flute

shots.action: 12 s. Scene 5, the journey. Seen from above, the land slides by beneath the flying flock in flat bands: dark forest and a river, then brown hills, then dry fields and small white houses. Day, night, day again in quick soft fades.
8 s. Long-Legs glides easily now, no puffing, steady among the others. No words.
10 s. Scene 6, the valley. A green valley full of shining ponds opens below. The big stork calls.
12 s. A great white spiral of storks pours down into the valley, turning, landing at the edges of the ponds; the camera follows Long-Legs down to the water.
8 s. Storks walk in the shallow edges and eat. Long-Legs looks around at so many storks. No words.
8 s. Evening in the valley: the ponds turn pink, and storks stand in long rows along the banks. A breath. No words.
9 s. Scene 7, the hill. Up on a dry hill, a girl lies on her tummy with binoculars; her grandfather sits on a folding stool with a notebook.
sound: a new, warm theme on guitar

shots.action: 10 s. The grandfather draws four upright lines and one across them in the notebook, slowly, then hands her the pencil.
11 s. The girl counts and draws, counts and draws; rows of little gates fill the page. She counts on the beat.
sound: five beats and a chime, again

shots.action: 9 s. Through the binoculars (a circle view): one young stork by a pond, standing on one leg, looking straight up at the hill.
8 s. She lowers the binoculars and waves. Far below, Long-Legs tilts his head. No words.
9 s. Scene 8, morning. Mist on the ponds; the storks wait. The sun warms the field and the faint stripes start to turn.
8 s. Long-Legs opens his wings first and steps into the warm air.
12 s. He circles up, and the others rise behind him into the same turning tower, round and round, up and up. The camera turns with them.
8 s. The turning tower of storks leans and drifts south; below, the ponds and the hill grow small. No words.
9 s. On the hill, the girl and her grandfather watch the slow white tower drift south.
sound: the warm theme and the waltz together

shots.action: 8 s. The girl draws one more stork in her notebook, smiling.

14 s. Closing image: an empty, bright morning sky with one last faint spiral far to the south, and the valley of shining ponds below. Nothing moves but the light. Hold the still picture 6 s while the music ends, then stop. No autoplay.
sound: the last notes of the flute

steps.picture: A child and a grown-up sit on a blanket in the shade of a tree in the early evening, both in sun hats, a water bottle beside them. The child draws three columns on a sheet of paper, with a small, a medium and a big bird drawn at the top of each.
The child looks up and points at a bird flying across the sky; the grown-up looks where the child points.
Close on the paper: the child draws one more tally line in the 'big bird' column; earlier marks are grouped as four upright lines with a fifth line across.
The child counts the tally gates in one column, a finger on each gate, lips moving.
The child circles the column with the most gates and grins; the grown-up holds up a thumb.
